newsitem.title: POLAND: Ex-communists, Solidarity party top Polish poll.
newsitem.headline: Ex-communists, Solidarity party top Polish poll.

text.p: Poland's ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) and the right-leaning Solidarity Electoral Action (AWS) led by the Solidarity trade union were tied for first place in the latest state television OBOP poll on Monday.
The OBOP poll, conducted May 8-10, showed both SLD and AWS with 24 percent support, with the radical right-wing Movement for Reconstruction of Poland (ROP) third with 12 percent backing.
In the May survey, support for the National Pensioners' Party (KPEiR) increased two points to 10 percent, the same backing as the Peasant Party (PSL).
The poll was conducted amoung 1,016 adult Poles. Poland is scheduled to hold parliamentary elections in September.
PARTY NAME MAY 8-10 APRIL 5-8
SLD 24 25
AWS 24 23
ROP 12 11
PSL 10 10
KPEiR 10 8
UW 9 11
UP 5 4
NOTE - Party names:
SLD - the Democratic Left Alliance, the ex-communist group and the larger partner in the ruling leftist coalition.
AWS - The Solidarity Electoral Action, an opposition electoral bloc of more than 30 small right-wing parties led by the Solidarity trade union.
ROP - The Movement for Reconstruction of Poland, a non-parliamentary group, advocating patriotic, anti-communist and often populist values.
PSL - The Polish Peasant Party, the smaller partner in the government coalition.
KPEiR - The National Pensioners' Party, a party lobbying pensioners' interests.
UW - The Union for Freedom, a right-centrist group, the biggest opposition party in parliament.
UP - The Union of Labour, a leftist opposition party.
